# NetAdapt-IoT field scheduling

The host selector uses the FUD-Ada score, frozen constants (1.0 and 2.5), eligibility and tie-breaking from [NetAdapt-IoT at c9f68d1](https://github.com/Sver0411/NetAdapt-IoT/blob/c9f68d11cec0c6c425fe98e2a054b2b0403743df/src/netadapt/ext/adaptive_scheduler.py#L28-L58). The upstream Python source has SHA-256 `a8860eed70463ebfbe04de30ca7bcb2b2c088a938bd8d16751fadc26aafc7c71`. The [MIT license](LICENSE) applies. The standalone scalar implementation uses Python's standard library to avoid loading the upstream simulator, NumPy, or a compiler in the seven-role demo. The selection test uses frozen choices from the upstream [C11 kernel](https://github.com/Sver0411/NetAdapt-IoT/blob/c9f68d11cec0c6c425fe98e2a054b2b0403743df/src/netadapt/c11/netadapt_sched.c).

The host adapter models one shared, work-conserving field outlet across directed routes. It keeps one FIFO for each source, destination and traffic class. The number of admitted attempts is bounded; full queues apply backpressure. Application retries, identities, command checks and durable receipt generation remain in the node processes. Field scheduling retains admitted telemetry and late events so the receiver can still record history and enforce command freshness.

Each dispatch occupies one logical slot per AL fragment at the configured MTU. Logical generation is the slot at scheduling ingress, including on retries. The four host traffic classes, weights, target ages and deadline budgets are defined in `common/lora/scheduled_transport.py`. They express relative priorities in fragment slots. This model counts simulated channel service under load; wall time, physical RF airtime, end-to-end sample age and power require separate measurements.

The upstream probability update uses simulated reassembly at the destination as its observed link outcome. The application still sends its normal ACKs and durable receipts. We advance bounded service debt over occupied slots for the current backlogged flow heads, normalize target shares across those heads, and use the actual head's fragment count as its service cost. The reference simulator uses a fixed population, configured per-flow cost, an optional duty-cycle budget and a loss calendar. The host adapter can send immediately whenever the modeled outlet is free. The FIFO comparison uses identical framing and capacity. The cloud socket continues using the existing TCP or separately selected uplink.
